stimuli.text: A solid insulating sphere of radius R = 0.18 m has a total charge Q = +2 nC distributed uniformly throughout its volume.
An initially uncharged 9 µF capacitor, a 140 kΩ resistor, an ideal 20 V battery and an open switch are connected in series. The switch is closed at t = 0.
Students measure the resistance of different lengths of a wire with a diameter of 0.4 mm, using a battery, an ammeter and a voltmeter.

A conducting rod of mass 0.5 kg and length 0.7 m slides without friction on horizontal rails connected by a 10 Ω resistor. A uniform 0.7 T magnetic field points vertically through the rails. The rod is given an initial speed of 10 m/s and then released.

questions.stem: How much work must an external agent do to move a +6 µC charge slowly from a point at -2 V to a point at 76 V?
A long straight wire carries a uniform charge of 3 µC/m. What is the field 0.42 m from it?

options.why: A line charge's field falls off as 1/r.
Correct. E = λ/(2πε₀r), from Gauss's law with a cylinder.

questions.stem: The current in a wire is $$I(t) = 3t$$ A. How much charge passes a point from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 4$$ s?
A battery with emf 8 V and internal resistance 0.3 Ω is connected to a 4 Ω resistor. What is the terminal voltage?

options.why: Some voltage is lost across the internal resistance.
That is the internal voltage drop.
Correct. I = ε/(R + r); V = ε − Ir.

questions.stem: Two point charges of 5 µC and −3 µC are 0.22 m apart. What is the magnitude of the force between them?
A solenoid 0.3 m long has 700 turns and carries 3 A. What is the magnetic field inside it?

options.why: Correct. B = μ₀nI with n = N/L.
That resembles a wire's field; use B = μ₀nI.

questions.stem: Point P is 0.3 m from a +3 µC charge and 0.2 m from a −3 µC charge. What is the electric potential at P?

options.why: Correct. Potential is a scalar: add kq/r with signs.
The negative charge contributes negative potential.

questions.stem: A 10 µF capacitor is in series with a parallel combination of 4 µF and 2 µF. What is the equivalent capacitance?

options.why: The series and parallel rules are swapped (they are the reverse of resistors).
Not all the capacitors are in series.
Correct. Capacitors add in parallel; reciprocals add in series.
Not all the capacitors are in parallel.

questions.stem: A 59 Ω resistor is connected across 40 V. What power does it dissipate?
A 14 µF capacitor is charged to 75 V. How much energy does it store?
An electron starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of 800 V. What is its final speed? ($$m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}$$ kg)
Two parallel plates 0.01 m apart have a potential difference of 80 V. What is the field between them?

options.why: Correct. In a uniform field, E = ΔV/d.

questions.stem: A ring of radius 0.24 m carries 5 µC spread uniformly. What is the field magnitude on its axis 0.24 m from the center?

options.why: The charge is not at the center.
Only the axial components add; the others cancel.

questions.stem: A battery with emf 6 V and internal resistance 0.9 Ω is connected to a 18 Ω resistor. What is the terminal voltage?

options.why: Some voltage is lost across the internal resistance.
That is the internal voltage drop.
Correct. I = ε/(R + r); V = ε − Ir.

questions.stem: A uniform field of 400 N/C passes through a flat 0.7 m² surface whose normal makes 30° with the field. What is the flux through the surface?

options.why: θ is measured from the normal, so use cos θ.

questions.stem: An electron moves at $$2 \times 10^{6}$$ m/s perpendicular to a uniform 0.16 T magnetic field. What is the radius of its path?

options.why: Correct. qvB = mv²/r, so r = mv/(qB).

questions.stem: An electron starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of 200 V. What is its final speed? ($$m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}$$ kg)
A parallel-plate capacitor has plates of area 0.06 m² separated by 1 mm of air. What is its capacitance?
A long straight wire carries 17 A. What is the magnetic field 0.14 m from it?

options.why: That is the field at the center of a loop.
A long wire's field falls off as 1/r.

questions.stem: A 30-turn coil of area 0.08 m² is perpendicular to a magnetic field that changes by 0.5 T in 0.1 s. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf?

options.why: Multiply by the number of turns.

questions.stem: A solid insulating sphere of radius 0.09 m has 4 µC distributed uniformly through its volume. What is the field magnitude 0.063 m from its center?

options.why: Correct. Inside, the enclosed charge is Q(r/R)³, so E = kQr/R³.
Only the charge inside radius r counts.
That is the field at the surface.

questions.stem: An ideal 13 V battery is connected at $$t = 0$$ to a 1 Ω resistor and a 0.5 H inductor in series. What is the current at $$t = 1.5$$ s?

options.why: The current has not reached its final value.
Correct. τ = L/R = 0.5 s; I = (ε/R)(1 − e^(−t/τ)).

questions.stem: Two long parallel wires 0.06 m apart carry 11 A and 6 A in the same direction. What is the force per meter between them?

options.why: Correct. F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd); parallel currents attract.
The force per length falls off as 1/d.
Parallel currents attract; antiparallel currents repel.

questions.stem: A flat circular coil of 6 turns and radius 0.04 m carries 17 A. What is the field at its center?

options.why: That is a straight wire's field.

questions.stem: The current in a 0.29 H inductor changes by 7 A in 0.04 s. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf?

options.why: That is power from energy; use ε = L dI/dt.

questions.stem: A 0.5 m wire carrying 9 A makes a 30° angle with a uniform 1 T magnetic field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on it?

options.why: Use sin θ, from the cross product.

questions.stem: A 1 µF capacitor is in parallel with a series combination of 2 µF and 10 µF. What is the equivalent capacitance?

options.why: Correct. Capacitors add in parallel; reciprocals add in series.
Not all the capacitors are in parallel.
The series and parallel rules are swapped (they are the reverse of resistors).
Not all the capacitors are in series.

questions.stem: A wire 3 m long has a diameter of 0.7 mm and resistivity $$2.8 \times 10^{-8}$$ Ω·m. What is its resistance?

options.why: Correct. R = ρL/A with A = π(d/2)².

questions.stem: Two identical small conducting spheres carry -3 µC and -2 µC. They are touched together and separated. What is the charge on each?

options.why: Correct. Identical conductors share the total charge equally.
The total is shared between two spheres.
Add the charges with their signs.

questions.explanation: Total -5 µC, split equally: -2.5 µC each.

questions.stem: An LC circuit has a 20 mH inductor and a 1 µF capacitor. What is its angular frequency ω of oscillation?
Charges of -5 µC, -5 µC, -2 µC sit at the corners of an equilateral triangle with sides 0.1 m. What is the system's electric potential energy?

options.why: Correct. Add kqᵢqⱼ/r for all three pairs.
Keep the signs of the charges.

questions.stem: A single loop contains a 23 V battery and a 15 V battery connected so their emfs oppose each other, plus resistors of 2 Ω and 4 Ω. What is the current?

options.why: Both resistors are in the loop.
Correct. Loop rule: ε₁ − ε₂ − I(R₁ + R₂) = 0.

questions.stem: Charges of +5 µC and +4 µC are 0.9 m apart. What is the magnitude of the electric field at the midpoint between them?

options.why: Check the directions of the two fields at the midpoint.
Correct. Like charges' fields point in opposite directions at the midpoint: subtract.
The distance is d/2, so r² = d²/4.
Each charge is d/2 from the midpoint.

questions.explanation: Each field is k q/(d/2)²: 2.22 \times 10^{5} and 1.78 \times 10^{5} N/C, opposite, giving 4.44 \times 10^{4} N/C.

questions.stem: A conducting sphere of radius 4 cm carrying 110 nC is connected by a long thin wire to an uncharged conducting sphere of radius 6 cm far away. What charge ends up on the smaller sphere?

options.why: Correct. Connected spheres reach equal potential, so Q ∝ R.
Equal potential gives Q ∝ R, not R².
That is the larger sphere's charge.

questions.explanation: kQ₁/R₁ = kQ₂/R₂ with Q₁ + Q₂ = 110: Q₁ = 44 nC.

questions.stem: A 1 µF capacitor starts uncharged and is charged through a 130 kΩ resistor by a 18 V battery. What is the capacitor's voltage after 0.39 s?

options.why: That is the charging resistor's voltage.
The change is exponential, not linear.
Correct. τ = RC = 0.13 s; V = ε(1 − e^(−t/τ)).
Convert kΩ and µF to Ω and F.

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor is charged and then disconnected from the battery. A dielectric with κ = 5 is inserted to fill the gap. What happens to the capacitor's charge?

options.why: Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.
Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.
Correct. Disconnected, Q is fixed and C rises by κ.
Decide first whether Q or V is held fixed.

questions.explanation: C becomes κC. Q fixed: V = Q/C and U = Q²/(2C) fall by κ.

questions.stem: The electric potential along the x-axis is $$V(x) = 90x^2$$ V. What is the x-component of the electric field at $$x = 0.5$$ m?
A 10 Ω resistor is in series with a parallel pair of 9 Ω and 5 Ω, connected to an ideal 16 V battery. What is the current in the 9 Ω resistor?

options.why: Correct. Reduce the parallel pair, add the series resistor, then work back.
Only part of the battery's voltage is across the pair.

questions.stem: A charge of +9q is at $$x = 0$$ and a charge of +q is at $$x = 6$$ m. At what point between them is the electric field zero?

options.why: Compare r², so take square roots.
The zero point is closer to the smaller charge.

questions.stem: A rectangular loop of length 0.9 m lies in the plane of a long straight wire carrying 11 A, parallel to it. Its near and far sides are 0.09 m and 0.12 m from the wire. What is the magnetic flux through the loop?

options.why: The field is not uniform across the loop.

parts.prompt: Using Gauss's law, derive expressions for the electric field magnitude inside (r < R) and outside (r > R) the sphere.

rubric.criterion: Spherical Gaussian surface; enclosed charge inside is Q(r/R)³.

parts.prompt: Calculate the field magnitude at r = 0.09 m and at r = 0.36 m.
Sketch (describe) a graph of E versus r from 0 to 3R.

rubric.criterion: Linear increase from 0 to a maximum at R, then 1/r² decrease.
rubric.example: Peak value kQ/R² = 555 N/C at r = R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the electric potential at the surface and at the center (V = 0 at infinity).

rubric.criterion: Center potential by integrating the inside field.

parts.prompt: Write the loop equation for the circuit and solve it to find q(t).
Calculate the time constant, the initial current and the final charge on the capacitor.
Sketch (describe) graphs of the capacitor's voltage and the current versus time.

rubric.criterion: Capacitor voltage rises from 0 toward ε, concave down.
Current decays exponentially from I₀ toward 0.
rubric.example: About 37% of I₀ at t = τ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the energy stored in the capacitor after a long time, and compare it with the energy supplied by the battery.

rubric.criterion: The battery supplies Qε, twice as much; half is dissipated in the resistor.

parts.prompt: Describe (draw) how the ammeter and voltmeter should be connected, and how R is determined.

rubric.criterion: Ammeter in series with the wire; voltmeter in parallel across it.
Keep the current small or brief so the wire does not heat up.

parts.prompt: Plot (describe) R versus L and draw a best-fit line. Calculate its slope.
Use the slope to calculate the resistivity of the wire.

rubric.criterion: Uses slope = ρ/A with A = π(d/2)².

parts.prompt: The students then use a wire of the same material with twice the diameter. Predict the new slope of R versus L and explain.

rubric.criterion: The slope becomes one quarter as large because the area quadruples.

questions.title: A sliding rod in a magnetic field

parts.prompt: Describe qualitatively how the rod's speed changes after it is released, and explain using Lenz's law.

rubric.criterion: The rod slows down, approaching zero.
rubric.example: Its speed decreases ever more slowly.

rubric.criterion: The induced current produces a magnetic force opposing the motion (Lenz's law).
rubric.example: The force opposes the change in flux.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the magnetic force on the rod in terms of B, L, v and R.

rubric.criterion: Uses ε = BLv and I = ε/R.

parts.prompt: Write and solve a differential equation for v(t).
Calculate the initial current, and explain where the rod's initial kinetic energy ends up.

rubric.criterion: All of the kinetic energy is dissipated as thermal energy in the resistor.
